AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors.summary: Mathlib already has the real-variable toolkit this roadmap asks for: the Schwartz space and Fourier transform on real inner-product spaces, Fourier inversion, Poisson summation for ℤ ⊂ ℝ, Mellin transforms with inversion, and differentiation under the integral. It also has Deligne's Γ_ℝ/Γ_ℂ, finite-ring Gauss sums and Dirichlet conductors, and the GL₁/ℚ global theory in classical theta–Mellin form (continuation, functional equation with Gauss-sum root number, Euler product, trivial-character pole, removal of Euler factors by change of level), as well as Hecke's continuation and functional-equation package for holomorphic cusp forms on arithmetic subgroups, which is the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case. Tau Ceti adds the discreteness of K in 𝔸_K, ideal-indexed Euler products over number fields, and Shimura's Hecke-ring structure for GL₂ (the polynomial p-local Hecke ring and the prime-power recurrence). Everything local-field-theoretic and adelic is missing: Schwartz–Bruhat spaces at finite places, standard additive characters and self-dual measures, adelic Poisson summation, Tate local zeta integrals and ε-factors, Hecke L-functions beyond ℚ, and all of Godement–Jacquet, Rankin–Selberg, Satake/L-group Euler factors and the interpolation interfaces. Neither library has smooth admissible representations of p-adic groups.

targets.target: local Schwartz–Bruhat spaces: locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places, Schwartz functions at real and complex places
targets.note: `SchwartzMap` (𝓢(E,F) on a real normed space) covers the archimedean places ℝ and ℂ ≅ ℝ². Neither library packages locally constant compactly supported functions on a nonarchimedean local field as a space; searches for Schwartz–Bruhat/Bruhat–Schwartz and for `LocallyConstant` with `HasCompactSupport` found nothing.

targets.target: Fourier transform on local fields with respect to a nontrivial additive character; self-duality of the local additive groups
targets.note: `Fourier.fourierIntegral e μ f` is defined for any commutative ring with a unitary character `AddChar 𝕜 Circle` and a measure, so a local-field transform can be written, but only the real inner-product-space case has theorems. No standard character x ↦ exp(2πi{Tr x}_p) of ℚ_p or its extensions, no self-dual Haar measure and no isomorphism F_v ≅ F_v^ exist. `Mathlib/NumberTheory/Padics/AddChar.lean` classifies p-adic-valued characters of ℤ_p (Amice), a different object. Tau Ceti classifies continuous characters of the circle only.

targets.target: restricted tensor-product adelic Schwartz–Bruhat space S(𝔸_F) = ⊗'_v S(F_v)
targets.note: The restricted product and 𝔸_K exist as topological rings. There is no restricted tensor product of local function spaces and no space of factorizable adelic test functions; searches for restricted tensor products found nothing in either library.

targets.target: Fourier inversion (local and adelic, including the reflected argument)
targets.note: Inversion is proved on finite-dimensional real inner-product spaces with the 2π convention, for integrable f with integrable 𝓕f (continuous or at continuity points). This covers the real and complex places; nothing covers nonarchimedean fields or 𝔸_F.

targets.target: change-of-character and change-of-measure formulas for local and adelic Fourier transforms
targets.note: Proved covariances are translation and linear isometries on real spaces, and Tau Ceti converts between the 2π Fourier convention and Mathlib's characteristic-function convention on real inner-product spaces. There is no formula relating the transforms for ψ and ψ(a·), and no rescaling of self-dual measures.

targets.target: adelic Poisson summation for the diagonal lattice F ⊂ 𝔸_F, with the volume of 𝔸_F/F
targets.note: Poisson summation is proved only for ℤ ⊂ ℝ: for continuous f with locally uniform summability of translates, and for Schwartz f. Tau Ceti proves K discrete and closed in 𝔸_K. Compactness of 𝔸_K/K (only mentioned in that file's docstring), its covolume, and any lattice or adelic Poisson formula are absent.

targets.target: holomorphic parameter integrals, Mellin transforms and the domination estimates that justify differentiating under the integral
targets.note: Differentiation of parametric integrals over any `RCLike` field (so holomorphic dependence), the Mellin transform on (0,∞) with convergence and holomorphy in s from rpow bounds, and Mellin inversion are all proved. They are real-line tools: no Mellin transform over F_v^× for finite v or over the idele class group is defined.

duplicates.note: Also builds adelic test functions as restricted tensor products of locally constant compactly supported functions at finite places (with C_c^∞ rather than Schwartz functions at infinity), so there should be a single restricted-tensor-product construction.

Defines the adelic Weil representation on the restricted tensor product of local Schwartz spaces and proves compatibility with changes of additive character, the same space and change-of-character formulas as AL.0.
The global-function-field counterpart: self-dual local characters and Haar measures from a differential, the residue pairing, discreteness and cocompactness of K ⊂ 𝔸_K, and adelic Poisson summation.
Also plans Mellin transforms and convergence proofs for interchanging limits, differentiation and Euler products, the analytic tools of AL.0's last sentence.

Declared supplier rather than overlap: it states discreteness of K in 𝔸_K and compactness of 𝔸_K/K, the lattice and covolume that AL.0's Poisson summation takes from GlobalNumberFields. Discreteness is already proved in Tau Ceti.

Builds Schwartz–Bruhat function spaces as the Schrödinger models of the Heisenberg extension, with polarizations and their change maps, local compactness, Haar normalization and the translation/modulation relations for a chosen Fourier convention: AL.0's local test-function spaces and change-of-character formulas, one layer below MP.4's adelic Weil representation.

targets.target: local Tate zeta integral Z(f,χ,s) = ∫ f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a quasi-character χ of F_v^× and a Schwartz–Bruhat f, convergent for Re s > 0
targets.note: At a real place and on ℝ_{>0}, the integral is Mathlib's Mellin transform, and ∫_0^∞ t^{a−1}e^{−rt} dt = r^{−a}Γ(a) is proved. There are no quasi-characters of F_v^× as objects, no multiplicative Haar measure d×x on a local field, and no nonarchimedean zeta integral.

targets.target: rationality of the nonarchimedean zeta integrals in q_v^{−s}
targets.note: No nonarchimedean zeta integral exists to be rational. Mathlib's `ofPowerSeries q f` only turns a formal power series in T = q^{−s} into a formal Dirichlet series.

targets.target: meromorphic continuation of the archimedean zeta integrals
targets.note: Continuation is available for Γ (hence for the Gaussian integral Γ_ℝ) and, abstractly, for Mellin transforms of Mathlib's weak FE-pairs (constant plus rapid decay, with f(1/x) = εx^k g(x)). There is no continuation of ∫_{ℝ^×} f(x)χ(x)|x|^s d×x for a general Schwartz f by Taylor expansion at 0, and no ℂ^× version.

targets.target: L-, ε- and γ-factors with exact normalizations and the local functional equation
targets.note: No local ε- or γ-factor and no local functional equation exist. `rootNumber` is the global root number of a Dirichlet character (Gauss sum over ZMod N divided by i^a√N), `gammaFactor` its archimedean factor, and the Γ_ℝ reflection identities are archimedean γ-factor ratios. None is obtained from a local integral.

targets.target: real and complex gamma factors Γ_ℝ(s) = π^{−s/2}Γ(s/2) and Γ_ℂ(s) = 2(2π)^{−s}Γ(s)
targets.note: Deligne's archimedean factors are in Mathlib with their doubling and reflection formulas, poles and residues. They are identified with the Mellin transform of a Gaussian theta sum (`hasSum_mellin_pi_mul_sq`), but not as the local zeta integral of the Gaussian against a character of ℝ^×.

targets.target: unramified and ramified characters of F_v^×, conductor exponents, Gauss sums and character twists
targets.note: Mathlib has Gauss sums over finite rings, with g(χ)g(χ⁻¹) = χ(−1)#R for nontrivial χ on a finite field, and conductors and primitive characters of Dirichlet characters. There is no unramified/ramified decomposition of characters of ℚ_p^× or K_v^×, no conductor exponent a(χ_v), and no local Gauss sum of a ramified character against ψ_v. Tau Ceti has only ring conductors (e.g. the conductor exponent of an order), not character conductors.

targets.target: global zeta integral: Euler factorization, meromorphic continuation and functional equation of Hecke L-functions via Poisson summation, keeping the trivial-character poles
targets.note: For F = ℚ and finite-order characters, Mathlib proves continuation, the functional equation with conductor, Gauss-sum root number and parity, the Euler product and the residue of the trivial character. It uses the classical Hurwitz/theta–Mellin route (with `completedRiemannZeta_one_sub` for ζ), not idelic integrals. Over a general number field there is only the Dedekind zeta series with its residue as a one-sided real limit (Mathlib) and its Euler product for Re s > 1 (Tau Ceti). No continuation or functional equation of Dedekind zeta or Hecke L-functions exists, and no idelic zeta integral.

duplicates.note: Continuation, functional equations with conductor, Gauss sum and parity, gamma factors and the principal-character pole for ζ and Dirichlet L-functions: the F = ℚ finite-order case of AL.1's global statements, which Mathlib largely has.
Completed Hecke and Dedekind L-functions over number fields with real/complex gamma factors, residues and ramified Euler factors, the same global targets as AL.1.

Defines Hecke characters as continuous characters of the idele class group, with local components, finite conductor and unitary part: the character carriers and conductors that AL.1 computes local factors for.
Classifies the continuous characters of ℝ^× and ℂ^× as |x|^s sgn(x)^ε and (z/|z|)^k|z|^s, the archimedean quasi-characters whose zeta integrals produce AL.1's real and complex gamma factors.

Proves Mellin-transform continuation, primitive-character Gauss sums, conductor change and imprimitive Euler-factor deletion, and the Dedekind-zeta pole, which it attributes to AL.1's trivial-character Tate theorem. These overlap AL.1's Dirichlet-character and trivial-character targets.
Proves the GL₁ dictionary with Hecke characters, including infinity type, conductor and unitary twist: the same character bookkeeping AL.1 does locally.

Builds prehomogeneous-vector-space zeta integrals and local densities with orbit decomposition, Poisson summation and functional equations, and lists AL.0 among its inputs: the same zeta-integral-to-functional-equation route as AL.1 for a different family, so the convergence and local-factor conventions must be shared.

targets.target: local Godement–Jacquet zeta integrals from Schwartz(–Bruhat) functions on M_n(E) and matrix coefficients of irreducible admissible representations of GL_n(E)
targets.note: Neither library has smooth or admissible representations of GL_n over a local field or their matrix coefficients; searches for admissible/smooth representation, matrix coefficient, Godement and Jacquet found nothing relevant. Only abstract Haar measure on locally compact groups and Schwartz functions on real vector spaces are available.

targets.target: nonarchimedean rationality in q^{−s}, the fractional-ideal characterization of L(s,π) and the local functional equation with γ(s,π,ψ)
targets.note: Nothing: no local zeta integrals, no fractional ideal of ℂ[q^{±s}] and no ε-factors for GL_n.

targets.target: archimedean gamma factors via Casselman–Wallach globalizations, Schwartz estimates and meromorphic parameter integrals; their functional equation
targets.note: No (g,K)-modules, Harish-Chandra modules or smooth Fréchet globalizations exist in either library (AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1 owns them).

targets.target: unramified spherical computation L(s,π) = det(1 − q^{−s}A_π)^{−1} and comparison with the Satake parameter
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves Shimura's Theorem 3.20 for n = 2 (and n = 1): the p-local Hecke ring of GL_n over ℚ relative to GL_n(ℤ) is a polynomial ring on the diagonal double cosets. It also proves the GL₂ recurrence T(p^{k+1}) = T(p)T(p^k) − p·T(p,p)T(p^{k−1}), the formal identity behind the degree-two Euler factor. There is no spherical function, Satake transform, unramified principal series or local zeta integral.

targets.target: global integral for cuspidal automorphic representations of GL_n: Euler factorization, analytic continuation and functional equation, with the n = 1 pole separated
targets.note: Only classical special cases exist, proved by Hecke's Mellin argument rather than adelic integrals. For n = 2 over ℚ and holomorphic modular forms on an arithmetic subgroup, Mathlib packages f(it) and its S-translate as a weak FE-pair (continuation and a functional equation relating f to f|S) and proves cusp-form L-functions entire; Tau Ceti identifies the coefficient L-series with them (`CuspForm.hasEntireExtension_qExpansion_coeff`). For a newform, Tau Ceti proves the formal Euler factorization at primes not dividing the level: a_{mn} = a_m a_n for coprime good m, n, and a_{p^{r+2}} = a_p a_{p^{r+1}} − χ(p)p^{k−1}a_{p^r}. The analytic Euler product is not stated. For n = 1 over ℚ there are Dirichlet L-functions. Nothing exists for n ≥ 3, for Maass forms or over other number fields.

targets.target: bounds and normalization conversions for use in interpolation formulas
targets.note: No GL_n local-factor normalizations exist to convert between.

duplicates.note: Relates the GL_n Hecke polynomial P_v(X) to the normalized Satake transform, determinant character and Tate twist: the unramified comparison AL.2 derives from the spherical zeta integral, so the two normalization dictionaries must coincide.

Hecke's completed L-function and functional equation for newforms of level N with the Atkin–Lehner sign, and their Euler product: the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case of AL.2's global Euler factorization and functional equation.

Constructs local constants for GL_m on the analytic side and proves their dictionary with Weil–Deligne constants. Its text assigns the integral constructions to AL, so its analytic L/ε-factors must be AL.2's rather than a second construction.

targets.target: comparison of the nonarchimedean Whittaker/derivative constructions of SR.5 with the classical complex Whittaker model
targets.note: No Whittaker functional, Kirillov model or Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivative exists in either library; the word Whittaker occurs only in bibliography entries for Whittaker–Watson.

targets.target: GL_n × GL_m local Rankin–Selberg integrals: convergence, nonarchimedean rationality and gcd-normalized L-factors
targets.note: Nothing. Searches for Rankin–Selberg, Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika and gcd L-factors found nothing; Tau Ceti's only 'Rankin' is Rankin's trick in an ideal-counting bound.

targets.target: archimedean Whittaker functionals with uniqueness and continuity on Casselman–Wallach globalizations, completed tensor products, and Jacquet's estimates (§§2–16)
targets.note: Mathlib has the injective seminorm on finite tensor products of normed spaces, but no completed projective tensor product of Fréchet spaces, no globalization and no Whittaker functional.

targets.target: archimedean holomorphic multiples, boundedness in vertical strips, gamma factors and functional equation without a gcd argument
targets.note: Only the general Phragmén–Lindelöf principle in a vertical strip is available as a tool; no Rankin–Selberg integral exists to apply it to.

targets.target: unramified computations, global unfolding for cuspidal data, poles in the contragredient/twist case and nonvanishing in the proved regions
targets.note: Mathlib defines only the Petersson integrand y^k f(τ)·conj f'(τ); there is no unfolding of an Eisenstein series against cusp forms and no Rankin–Selberg L-function.

targets.target: comparison of integral rational structures, Gauss sums and complex periods with the cohomological normalization; periods up to their scalar ambiguity
targets.note: Finite-ring Gauss sums exist, but there is no period of an automorphic representation, no cohomological normalization and no rational structure to compare.

duplicates.note: Defines period lines and scalar periods Ω_f^± of a newform up to basis choice, with Gauss sums and critical values of twists: the GL₂ × GL₁ case of AL.3's period comparison and scalar-ambiguity requirement.
Proves a Rankin–Selberg/Hecke evaluation of the regulator integral for modular units at a stated level and character, a specific GL₂ × GL₂ unfolding that should consume AL.3 rather than reprove it.

Declared supplier: builds the Bernstein–Zelevinsky derivatives and Whittaker functionals AL.3 imports. The comparison with the classical complex Whittaker model sits on the boundary and should have one owner.

targets.target: Euler polynomial det(1 − r(t_v)X) attached to the Satake semisimple conjugacy class t_v and an algebraic representation r of the L-group
targets.note: `Matrix.charpolyRev M = det(1 − X·M)` supplies the polynomial once a matrix is given. No L-group, no Satake class and no representation of a dual group exist in either library; searches for Satake, L-group, Langlands dual and dual group found nothing.

targets.target: invariance of the Euler polynomial under conjugacy, direct sum, tensor product, duality and scalar extension
targets.note: The linear algebra for conjugacy, direct sums and base change is in Mathlib for characteristic polynomials (hence for their reverses). There is no formula for the characteristic polynomial of a tensor product or of the contragredient in terms of the factors, and nothing ties these to Satake parameters.

targets.target: partial Euler product L^S(s,π,r) and its convergence under a supplied bound on the Satake eigenvalues
targets.note: Mathlib builds formal L-functions from local power series in q^{−s} (`ofPowerSeries`, `eulerProduct`) and proves ∏_p Σ_e f(p^e) = Σ f(n) for multiplicative f with absolutely summable values. Tau Ceti has the ideal-indexed Euler product of a multiplicative weight over a number field, and the degree-two good-prime recurrence of newform coefficients (the standard L-function of GL₂/ℚ in formal form). The step from an eigenvalue bound |α_{v,i}| ≤ q_v^θ to absolute convergence of a degree-n Euler product for Re s > 1 + θ is not proved, and no L^S(s,π,r) is defined.

targets.target: comparison with the AL.1–AL.3 factors and with Weil–Deligne L-factors under an actual local-compatibility theorem
targets.note: No Weil group, Weil–Deligne representation or local L-factor of a Galois representation exists in either library, and no AL.1–AL.3 factors exist to compare.

duplicates.note: For GL_n and its standard representation, constructs the Hecke polynomial Σ(−1)^i q^{i(i−1)/2}T_{v,i}X^{n−i} and relates it to normalized Satake: the same unramified Euler polynomial as AL.4 in that case.
Builds the normalization dictionary among normalized Satake, the integral Hecke polynomial, Frobenius conventions and Tate twists, the conventions AL.4's Euler polynomials must follow.
Defines completed L-functions from local Weil–Deligne data, the Galois-side factors AL.4 is to compare with.

targets.target: removal and reinsertion of Euler factors at a finite set, and imprimitive/primitive comparisons
targets.note: For Dirichlet characters Mathlib proves L(χ at level N, s) = L(χ, s)·∏_{p∣N}(1 − χ(p)p^{−s}) as entire or meromorphic functions, and identifies a character with the change of level of its primitive character. Tau Ceti restricts ideal weights away from a finite set of primes and proves finite Euler products for the supported part. Nothing exists for GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions.

targets.target: critical-value normalization, functional-equation sign and algebraicity inputs for the GL₂ and Rankin families of AutomorphicPadicLFunctions
targets.note: Only GL₁/ℚ analogues exist: rationality of ζ(−k) via Bernoulli numbers and the root number of a Dirichlet character. No critical values, periods or signs of GL₂ or Rankin–Selberg L-functions are formalized.

targets.target: compatibility of conductor exponents, local test vectors and character twists
targets.note: No local conductor exponent of a representation, no newvector or test vector, and no twisting of local representations exists.

targets.target: explicit limiting or derivative results for vanishing Euler factors (exceptional zeros), without cancellation
targets.note: Nothing on exceptional zeros or L-invariants in either library.

targets.target: export of the formulas both as formal local polynomials and as complex evaluations
targets.note: Mathlib's route from local polynomials, through `PowerSeries.invOfUnit` and `ofPowerSeries`/`eulerProduct`, to `LSeries` provides the formal-versus-complex carriers. The GL₂ and Rankin formulas to export do not exist.

duplicates.note: Proves conductor change, imprimitive Euler-factor deletion and algebraicity of the complex values for Dirichlet characters: AL.5's removal/reinsertion and algebraicity interfaces for GL₁.
Primitive/imprimitive comparisons, conductor change and the interpolation formula with its removed Euler factor (1 − (χη)(p)p^{k−1}), the GL₁ instance of AL.5's contracts.
Proves changes of periods, coefficients and primitive/imprimitive conventions across the p-adic constructions, the consumer-side twin of AL.5's normalization interfaces.
States the GL₂ interpolation formula with its Euler factor (1 − χ(p)p^j/α), Gauss sum, (2πi)^{j+1} and period normalization, the critical-value normalization AL.5 is to supply.
Formulates normalized critical values with signs and powers of 2πi and retains ramified and imprimitive corrections: the same normalization targets from the periods side.

AutomorphicSpectralTheory.summary: The libraries supply general tools but no automorphic spectral theory. Mathlib has Fubini and the sum/derivative–integral interchange lemmas, Hilbert direct sums, the spectral theorem for compact self-adjoint operators and the continuous functional calculus, test-function and Schwartz spaces with tempered distributions, norm-meromorphic Banach-valued functions, the unfolding trick for quotient measures, and holomorphic Eisenstein series of weight k ≥ 3 for Γ(N). Tau Ceti adds unbounded self-adjoint operators with Stone's theorem, compact self-adjoint convolution operators and the Peter–Weyl theorem (the discrete decomposition of L²(G) for compact G), Petersson products on finite-index subgroups, the classical multiplicity-one and nebentypus decompositions, the Casimir element and Verma central characters, dynamic parabolic subgroups with Levi decomposition on points, and the Frobenius formula for induced characters of finite groups. Everything the roadmap names is missing: direct integrals, trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt kernels, nuclear test-function spaces, weakly or strongly meromorphic operator families, normalized parabolic induction, Eisenstein series and intertwining operators for reductive groups with their continuation, Arthur truncation and Maass–Selberg, the spectral decomposition of L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)), Franke's weighted cohomology, and every part of the coarse, fine and invariant trace formula. Only AS.0's interchange lemmas are fully present.

targets.target: measurable fields of separable Hilbert spaces, direct integrals, decomposable operators and isometric integration maps
targets.note: Only the two extreme cases exist. One is Hilbert direct sums (`IsHilbertSum`: an orthogonal family with E ≅ ℓ²(G)), the counting-measure case. The other is L²(α,μ;E) for a single fixed Hilbert space E, the constant-field case. Tau Ceti builds Hilbert bases of L² of product measures. There is no measurable field of Hilbert spaces, no direct integral, and no decomposable operator; searches for direct integral, measurable field and Hilbert bundle found nothing.

targets.target: the spectral theorem needed for the spectrum (bounded normal and unbounded self-adjoint operators, in projection-valued or multiplication-operator form), reusing compact-operator spectral theory
targets.note: The compact self-adjoint spectral theorem is complete: eigenspaces are dense in Mathlib, and Tau Ceti builds a Hilbert basis of eigenvectors. There is also the continuous functional calculus for normal elements of C*-algebras. For unbounded operators, Tau Ceti has partial linear maps with adjoints, self-adjointness, nonreal points in the resolvent set, and Stone's theorem (self-adjoint A ↔ unitary C₀-group generated by iA). No projection-valued measure, spectral measure or multiplication-operator form of the spectral theorem exists, bounded or unbounded.

targets.target: trace-class and Hilbert–Schmidt integral operators (kernels, traces as diagonal integrals)
targets.note: Neither library defines trace-class, Hilbert–Schmidt, nuclear or Schatten operators; Mathlib mentions trace-class only in a TODO of the multivariate Gaussian file. Tau Ceti proves convolution by a continuous kernel is compact on L²(G) for compact G, and tr π(f) = ∫ f·χ_π for finite-dimensional π.

targets.target: nuclear Fréchet test-function spaces
targets.note: Mathlib has C^n test functions 𝓓^n(Ω,F) with the LF topology, the spaces 𝓓_K and the Schwartz space as locally convex (Schwartz also first countable) spaces on real normed spaces. It proves neither completeness (Fréchet) nor nuclearity, and has no test functions on a Lie group or on G(𝔸).

targets.target: weakly and strongly meromorphic operator-valued families and their finite-rank residues
targets.note: `MeromorphicAt` and holomorphy apply to functions into any normed space, including E →L[ℂ] F, so norm-meromorphic operator families are covered. Tau Ceti proves the resolvent of a partial linear map analytic, and Mathlib has the Fredholm alternative for a single compact operator. There is no weak or strong meromorphy, no analytic Fredholm theorem in a parameter, and no residue theory for operator families (Tau Ceti's residues are scalar).

targets.target: Fubini and interchange lemmas (sums, integrals, derivatives) under integrability hypotheses
targets.note: Fubini for s-finite measures, sum–integral interchange for countable families with summable L¹ norms, and differentiation under the integral (over any `RCLike` parameter, so holomorphic dependence is included) are all in Mathlib, with explicit integrability hypotheses.

targets.target: distributional convergence
targets.note: Tempered distributions carry the pointwise-convergence topology, with convergence tested on each Schwartz function, and distributions 𝓓' on open subsets of real normed spaces carry the compact-convergence topology. There are no distributions on C_c^∞ of a locally compact group or of G(𝔸), which is what the trace-formula distributions need.

duplicates.note: Builds compact self-adjoint convolution (integral) operators on L²(G) with finite-dimensional eigenspaces and a spectral decomposition. This is the compact-group instance of AS.0's integral-operator and compact spectral-theory toolkit, already completed in Tau Ceti.

targets.target: sections of normalized parabolic induction from cuspidal data on a rational Levi M, depending holomorphically on λ ∈ a*_{M,ℂ}
targets.note: Only ingredients exist. Mathlib has algebraic (unnormalized) coinduction and the modular character of a locally compact group, from which δ_P could be built (its continuity is a TODO). Tau Ceti has the dynamic parabolic P(λ) of a cocharacter of an affine group scheme with Levi decomposition U(λ) ⋊ Z(λ) on points, and unnormalized principal series of GL₂(𝔽_q). There is no smooth induced representation of G(𝔸), no a*_M, and no holomorphic family of sections.

targets.target: absolute and locally uniform convergence of the Eisenstein series Σ_{P(F)\G(F)} φ_λ(γg) in a positive chamber, with differentiated growth estimates and automorphy
targets.note: Only the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ case at an integral point: Mathlib's Eisenstein series of weight k ≥ 3 for Γ(N) (a sum over coprime pairs in a congruence class) converges locally uniformly, is Γ(N)-invariant, bounded at every cusp, and a modular form. There is no complex parameter s or λ, no non-holomorphic or Maass Eisenstein series (searches for these, Epstein zeta and Godement's criterion found nothing), and nothing for a parabolic of a general reductive group.

targets.target: constant term of the Eisenstein series along a parabolic as a finite Weyl-group sum of intertwining operators in the convergence region
targets.note: Mathlib computes q-coefficients (including the constant term) as integrals over a period and shows the normalized E_k has constant term 1. There is no constant term along a unipotent radical of G(𝔸), no intertwining operator, and no Weyl-sum formula.

duplicates.note: Proves convergence in the initial chamber and constant terms of genuine Eisenstein series on a double cover of GSp(4). Its text requires adapting AS's linear-group estimates rather than importing them, so this is a parallel development for covers.

Plans the translation between Mathlib's level-Γ(N) holomorphic Eisenstein series and Eisenstein series with character. That is the classical GL₂/ℚ holomorphic special case of AS.1's convergence and automorphy statements.

targets.target: global and local standard intertwining operators M(w,λ) by convergent unipotent integrals; factorization for factorizable sections; cocycle and adjoint identities
targets.note: Only algebraic intertwiners and the finite-group Mackey theory exist: the double-coset decomposition of Res∘Ind and the Mackey formula for dim Hom between induced representations, the finite analogue of the Bruhat-cell analysis of intertwiners. There are no unipotent integrals, no Gindikin–Karpelevich formula and no cocycle relation.

targets.target: meromorphic continuation of intertwining operators and Eisenstein series, functional equations, and regularity/unitarity on the unitary axis, tracking singular hyperplanes and residues
targets.note: The only continuation machinery is the one-variable Mellin/theta argument for L-functions (weak FE-pairs, completed ζ and Dirichlet L-functions), which gives the scalar ξ(s) that appears in the SL₂(ℤ) scattering coefficient. Nothing continues an Eisenstein series or an operator family in λ.

targets.target: normalizing factors and normalized intertwining operators
targets.note: No normalizing factors or local coefficients (Langlands–Shahidi) exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Proves meromorphic continuation of cover-specific Eisenstein series through prescribed intertwining operators, with their functional equations and residues: AS.2's targets on a nonlinear cover.

targets.target: Arthur's truncation operator Λ^T from parabolic constant terms and chamber indicators τ̂_P; local finiteness and the alternating-sum identities on root cones (Langlands' combinatorial lemma)
targets.note: Only neighbouring objects exist: the height-truncated SL₂(ℤ) fundamental domain (a set, not an operator), the dominant chamber of a root system in Tau Ceti, and the lemma that pairwise obtuse vectors in a half-space are linearly independent (a root-cone input). There is no τ_P or τ̂_P and no truncation operator.

targets.target: integrability (rapid decay) of truncated automorphic forms for sufficiently regular T
targets.note: For classical forms there are measure-theoretic fundamental domains for PSL₂(ℤ), moderate growth of modular forms on arithmetic subgroups, and exponential decay of cusp forms at i∞. There are no Siegel sets for general G (reduction theory is AdelicAlgebraicGroups AA.3) and no truncated automorphic forms.

targets.target: polynomial-exponential dependence of truncated integrals on T and the behaviour of the coefficients
targets.note: No exponential polynomials in T or extraction of their coefficients exist.

targets.target: Maass–Selberg inner-product formula for truncated Eisenstein series, with limits at singular parameters, and the orthogonality and norm identities for wave packets
targets.note: Tau Ceti has Petersson products of cusp forms on finite-index subgroups, independent of the fundamental domain. Mathlib has the unfolding trick ∫_G g(πx) f(x) = ∫_{G/Γ} g·automorphize f. Nothing concerns Eisenstein series or wave packets.

targets.target: discrete cuspidal and residual subspaces of L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)) and Eisenstein wave packets
targets.note: Only holomorphic cusp forms as a submodule of M_k(Γ), and Petersson-orthogonal complements inside S_k(Γ), exist. There is no L² space on an adelic quotient, no residual spectrum and no wave packet.

targets.target: unitary isomorphism from the sum/direct integral over associate cuspidal data onto L², with surjectivity, Weyl multiplicity factors and separation of residual and continuous terms
targets.note: Nothing; this needs AS.0's direct integrals and AS.1–AS.3, none of which exist.

targets.target: finite multiplicities in the discrete spectrum
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves classical multiplicity one (good-Hecke eigenspaces in S_k(N,χ)^new have dimension ≤ 1) and finite-dimensionality of nonzero eigenspaces of convolution operators on compact groups. Finite multiplicity of automorphic representations in L²_disc is not stated.

targets.target: compatibility of the decomposition with finite Hecke operators and central characters
targets.note: Classically, Tau Ceti decomposes S_k(Γ₁(N)) into Petersson-orthogonal nebentypus spaces (the central-character decomposition for holomorphic forms) and proves Shimura's commutativity criterion for Hecke rings. No Hecke or central-character action on L²(G(F)\G(𝔸)) is defined.

targets.target: compact quotients: specialization to a discrete Hilbert sum with finite multiplicities
targets.note: For a compact group G and trivial Γ, Tau Ceti proves Peter–Weyl: the normalized matrix coefficients of a set of unitary irreducible representatives form a Hilbert basis of L²(G), so the right regular representation is a discrete Hilbert sum with multiplicity dim V. The Gelfand–Graev–Piatetski-Shapiro theorem for compact Γ\G with noncompact G (e.g. anisotropic groups) is absent.

targets.target: GL₂ over ℚ: recovery of the continuous Eisenstein contribution
targets.note: No non-holomorphic Eisenstein series, Maass forms or Laplacian spectrum on SL₂(ℤ)\ℍ exist in either library.

duplicates.note: Deduces square integrability of cusp forms with unitary central character and finite multiplicity of cuspidal constituents, the cuspidal part of AS.4's finite-multiplicity statement.
The Peter–Weyl Hilbert basis of L²(G) for compact G is the trivial-Γ case of AS.4's compact-quotient specialization. It is already completed in Tau Ceti and should be reused.
Builds the Petersson inner product with Hecke adjoints and a simultaneous orthonormal eigenbasis of S_k(Γ₁(N)): the holomorphic GL₂/ℚ piece of the discrete spectrum with Hecke compatibility.

targets.target: weighted L² complexes and regularization
targets.note: Searches for weighted cohomology, weighted L² complexes and regularization found nothing.

targets.target: finite-infinitesimal-character functors (Z(g)-finite parts)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has the algebraic inputs: the Casimir element is central in U(L) for a nondegenerate Killing form, central characters χ_λ : Z(U(L)) → K come from Verma modules, and the Casimir acts on a highest-weight module by ⟨λ+ρ,λ+ρ⟩ − ⟨ρ,ρ⟩. The Harish-Chandra isomorphism, generalized Z(g)-eigenspace functors and Z(g)-finite function spaces are absent.

targets.target: filtration and acyclicity theorems comparing relative Lie algebra cohomology of automorphic forms with that of smooth functions of uniform moderate growth (Franke)
targets.note: Mathlib has Lie algebra cochains only in degrees ≤ 3 (with the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex listed as TODO) and group cohomology. There are no (g,K)-modules, no relative Lie algebra cohomology and no Franke filtration.

targets.target: automorphic comparison with algebraic coefficient systems and Hecke equivariance, keeping ordinary rather than cuspidal or L² cohomology
targets.note: Only local coefficient systems on the fundamental groupoid (Tau Ceti) and the abstract Hecke ring of double cosets (Mathlib) exist. No cohomology of locally symmetric spaces carries a Hecke action.

duplicates.note: Constructs U(g_C), its centre, generalized infinitesimal-character subspaces and relative Lie algebra cochains Hom_K(∧^q(g/k),V), the objects on which AS.5's finite-infinitesimal-character functors and comparison are built.

Its full (late) form compares Betti, de Rham and relative Lie algebra cohomology and uses AS.5 for the automorphic step. The boundary between the de Rham comparison there and Franke's comparison here must be kept exact.

targets.target: automorphic kernel K_f(x,y) = Σ_{γ∈G(F)} f(x⁻¹γy) of R(f) for compactly supported smooth f, and its truncation
targets.note: Tau Ceti has convolution kernels (k∗f)(x) = ∫ k(xy⁻¹)f(y)dy and integrated operators π(f) for compact groups, and Mathlib has folding ∫_G f = ∫_{G/Γ} Σ_γ f(γx). No kernel of R(f) on L²(Γ\G) or G(F)\G(𝔸) exists, truncated or not.

targets.target: integrability and equality of the coarse geometric and spectral expansions
targets.note: Only the finite-group Frobenius formula for induced characters exists, the trace formula for a finite group. Searches for trace formula, Selberg and orbital integral found only unrelated uses (trace formulas in linear algebra and topology). The compact-quotient Selberg trace formula is also absent.

targets.target: weighted orbital integrals, weighted characters, (G,M)-families, their convergence and the fine expansions
targets.note: Nothing: no orbital integral of any kind is defined in either library.

targets.target: invariant distributions by the invariantization recursion and the invariant trace formula with its summation and convergence conditions
targets.note: For compact groups Tau Ceti proves tr π(f) = ∫ f·χ_π and that irreducible characters form a Hilbert basis of class functions, the compact analogue of characters as invariant distributions. There are no invariant distributions on G(𝔸) or on p-adic or real reductive groups.

duplicates.note: Builds the twisted invariant trace identity 'from the same kernel/truncation machinery' as AS.6 and says the untwisted formula is only a template, so the kernel, truncation and invariantization steps should be shared.
Constructs quotient measures on centralizer quotients and proves convergence of regular semisimple orbital integrals, the local harmonic analysis AS.6 asks to make reusable.
The Eichler–Selberg trace formula for Hecke operators at level one, with Hurwitz class numbers: a classical special case of the trace identity, planned by a separate elementary route.
Plans Selberg trace-formula comparisons and spectral zeta functions on compact or finite-volume quotients, overlapping AS.6's compact-quotient worked example.

CompletedCohomologyPartII.summary: The general homological algebra this roadmap leans on is largely in Mathlib and Tau Ceti. Group cohomology is Ext in Rep k G, for groups with torsion and with Shapiro's lemma. Filtered colimits of modules are exact, invariant under cofinal functors, and homology commutes with them (Tau Ceti). Mathlib has adic completion of modules with completeness and exactness, Mittag-Leffler systems of sets, Pontryagin duals with compact↔discrete topologies, derived categories with distinguished triangles, group homology as Tor, and continuous cohomology of topological groups. Tau Ceti adds smooth discrete representations with open stabilizers, continuous cohomology of profinite groups in degrees ≤ 2 (inflation–restriction, corestriction with cor∘res = index, Shapiro, the colimit over finite quotients), the Mackey decomposition, abstract Hecke rings with a commutativity criterion, and quotient covering maps with deck groups. Nothing specific to completed cohomology exists: no arithmetic quotients or towers, no lim¹ or Milnor sequence, no completed group rings O[[K]] or Lazard noetherianity, no cellular chains, no Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence, no compactly supported or boundary cohomology, no p-adic Banach or admissible representations, no Shimura varieties. Only CC.0's group-cohomology model and CC.1's colimit exactness are genuinely present.

targets.target: indexing categories of levels: compact open subgroups K_p with inclusions and conjugation, and cofinal normal or pro-p sequences
targets.note: Mathlib has the lattice of open (normal) subgroups and, in compact totally disconnected groups, open normal subgroups inside every neighbourhood of 1. Tau Ceti gives a cofinal antitone sequence of open normal subgroups in a topologically finitely generated compact group, a pro-p predicate, and the unit filtration 1+𝔪^i of a local field as a basis of neighbourhoods (the GL₁ congruence tower). There are no compact open subgroups of G(ℚ_p) for reductive G (GL_n(ℤ_p), principal congruence K(pⁿ)), no proof that these are pro-p, and no category of levels with conjugation maps.

targets.target: finite covering correspondences Y(K′) → Y(K) between arithmetic quotients, with composition identities and conjugation maps; neat cofinal towers that keep stabilizers at descended levels
targets.note: The topology of quotient coverings is available. A free, properly discontinuous action on a locally compact Hausdorff space gives a quotient covering (Mathlib). The intermediate map E/H → E/G for H ≤ G is a covering and deck transformations of E/H → X are N(H)/H (Tau Ceti). Arithmetic subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) act properly discontinuously on ℍ. There are no locally symmetric spaces Y(K) = G(ℚ)\G(𝔸)/K, no neat subgroups (Minkowski/Selberg lemmas are absent) and no orbifold or stack model at non-neat levels.

targets.target: derived group-cohomology model at levels with stabilizers, retaining torsion, with change of level
targets.note: Mathlib's group cohomology of an arbitrary group G with coefficients in a k-linear representation is Extⁿ_{Rep k G}(k, A), so it is the derived model and keeps all torsion of groups with torsion. Shapiro's lemma Hⁿ(G, Coind_S^G A) ≅ Hⁿ(S, A) holds for every subgroup, and Ind ≅ Coind for finite index, giving the level-change isomorphisms. Tau Ceti has the profinite Shapiro lemma in degree 1. The model is present for any group; what is missing is its input: the arithmetic groups Γ_K of a reductive group at each level (only congruence subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) exist), and the identification with the cohomology of the orbifold Γ_K\X (see the comparison target).

targets.target: compact support via compatible compactifications (Borel–Serre) or the functorial j_! model, with trace maps
targets.note: Group-side traces exist in low degree: corestriction on continuous H¹ for open finite-index subgroups (Tau Ceti), corestriction on group homology in all degrees (Mathlib), and the trace of modular forms between levels. There is no compactly supported cohomology, no Borel–Serre compactification, no extension by zero j_! and no transfer for finite covering spaces.

targets.target: comparison of singular, cellular and étale finite-coefficient models under finite-type/characteristic hypotheses
targets.note: Each model exists separately in some form: singular homology (Mathlib) and relative singular homology (Tau Ceti), sheaf cohomology on a site, and pro-étale Hⁿ(X, ℤ_ℓ). There is no singular cohomology with coefficients as a cochain theory, no cellular homology, no small étale cohomology with finite coefficients, and no comparison theorem between any two of them.

duplicates.note: Constructs the finite covering maps for nested compact opens at neat level, computes their degrees from stabilizer indices, proves Cartesian diagrams for Hecke correspondences and keeps quotient groupoids at non-neat level: the same covering-correspondence and stabilizer targets as CC.0.
Defines singular, cellular and compact-support cochains on the arithmetic quotients and proves their comparison with sheaf cohomology, which is CC.0's model comparison at finite level.

Constructs the p-level inverse systems, proves cofinality of the principal congruence systems and the group actions with level changes for Shimura towers: CC.0's indexing and conjugation data in the Shimura setting.
Assembles direct and inverse systems in tame and p-power level with restriction, corestriction and Hecke actions, and reexports CC's limits. The finite-level tower data overlaps CC.0.

Constructs the Borel–Serre compactification: rational parabolic boundary components, the manifold-with-corners structure at neat level, compactness of the quotient, the homotopy equivalence from the interior and the stratification spectral sequence. That is the compactification CC.0's compact-support target names, and the neat-level hypothesis CC.0's cofinal towers require.

targets.target: filtered colimits at fixed s in modules and complexes: exactness and independence under cofinal restriction
targets.note: Mathlib: AB5 for ModuleCat R (an unnamed instance in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/AB.lean), exactness of colim under exact colimits of shape J, the direct limit of modules, and colimit(F ⋙ G) ≅ colimit G for final F. Tau Ceti: AB5 without universe restrictions, and homology of homological complexes commutes with colimits of any exact shape, so the colimit of the complexes computes the colimit of cohomology. The tower cohomology to which these apply does not exist (CC.0).

targets.target: action of the full local group on colim_K Hⁱ by conjugating levels, with open stabilizers so that the action is smooth
targets.note: The notion of a smooth action is present: continuity of an action on a discrete space ↔ open stabilizers (Mathlib); smooth discrete representations and M = ⋃_U M^U for profinite groups (Tau Ceti); the conjugation action of G on H¹(N, M) for normal N (Tau Ceti). The action of G(ℚ_p) on the colimit of tower cohomology, which needs non-normal levels and all degrees, is absent.

targets.target: commuting tame Hecke operators from double-coset correspondences with explicit pullback/trace normalization
targets.note: Abstract Hecke rings of double cosets exist, with product, associativity, degree and Shimura's commutativity criterion via an anti-involution (Tau Ceti), and classical double-coset operators act on modular forms. No Hecke correspondence acts on the cohomology of arithmetic quotients, and no pullback/trace normalization is set up.

targets.target: Mackey and restriction/corestriction identities with degree factors, without inverting them integrally
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the Mackey decomposition Res_K Ind_H A ≅ ⨁_{KsH} Ind Res(ˢA) with no finiteness hypothesis. It also proves cor∘res = [G:U] on continuous cohomology in degrees 0, 1 and 2 (and on Tate cohomology in degrees 0 and −1). Mathlib has restriction in all degrees but no cohomological corestriction. cor∘res = index in all degrees, and the double-coset formula res∘cor on cohomology, are absent.

duplicates.note: Constructs Hecke correspondences on the finite-level complexes through K∩gKg⁻¹ with pullback and trace, composition via the double-coset algebra and change of level: the same Hecke-operator target as CC.1, before passing to the colimit.
Proves restriction/corestriction identities and descent consequences for the generic continuous cohomology theory, the generic form of CC.1's restriction/corestriction identities.
Declared supplier: defines smoothness by open stabilizers and proves closure under filtered colimits, which CC.1 applies to the colimit of tower cohomology.

targets.target: inverse systems in s and their topological inverse limit as an O-module, with separatedness and completeness
targets.note: Mathlib has the I-adic completion of a module as compatible sequences in M/IⁿM, which is I-adically complete (separated and precomplete) for finitely generated I. For rings it has the equivalence with topological completeness, and limits of topological modules with the limit topology (unnamed instances in Algebra/Category/ModuleCat/Topology/Basic.lean). The limit lim_s colim_K Hⁱ(Y(K), O/ϖ^s) itself, and a proof that this limit is ϖ-adically separated and complete, are absent.

targets.target: derived inverse limit of complexes, the lim¹ functor and the Milnor exact sequence 0 → lim¹ H^{i−1} → Hⁱ(R lim) → lim Hⁱ → 0
targets.note: No lim¹, derived limit, homotopy limit or Milnor sequence exists in either library; searches for lim1, lim¹, limOne, Milnor, holim and R lim found nothing. Mathlib's general right derived functors have not been applied to lim.

targets.target: surjectivity and Mittag-Leffler criteria for the vanishing of lim¹ at each use
targets.note: The Mittag-Leffler condition and its eventual-range consequences are formalized for functors to Type, and an ℕᵒᵖ-system with surjective transitions has lim → X₀ surjective. There is no Mittag-Leffler condition for module systems and no theorem that it kills lim¹, since lim¹ is not defined.

targets.target: comparison of the reduction of the completed module with its finite-coefficient counterpart under torsion/control hypotheses, with counterexample tests
targets.note: For modules Mathlib proves ker(M̂ → M/IⁿM) = Iⁿ·M̂ (I finitely generated) and exactness of completion on finite modules over a noetherian ring, and group cohomology has the long exact sequence usable for 0 → M → M → M/ϖ → 0. No comparison for completed cohomology or its reductions exists.

targets.target: the unitary Banach module obtained by inverting p on a complete bounded integral lattice, and continuity of the group and Hecke actions
targets.note: Only finite-rank lattice rationalization K ⊗ S ≅ V (Tau Ceti) and separately continuous representations (Mathlib) exist. There are no p-adic Banach representations and no unit-ball lattices; the separately continuous `ContRepresentation` does not give joint continuity of the action.

duplicates.note: The declared generic owner: constructs derived inverse limits and keeps lim¹ until a proved Mittag-Leffler condition removes it. CC.2's derived-limit and lim¹ targets are its targets applied to towers.
Proves the Mittag-Leffler and lim¹ statements before interchanging cohomology and inverse limits for lattices and their torsion quotients, the same interchange discipline as CC.2.
Proves derived Mittag-Leffler comparisons and keeps lim¹ for inverse systems of complexes over complete local rings, overlapping CC.2's derived-limit and Mittag-Leffler targets.

Defines p-completion as the derived inverse limit of the E/p^r system and constructs the Milnor lim¹ exact sequence together with the hypotheses under which it collapses to an ordinary inverse limit: CC.2's derived-limit, lim¹ and Milnor-sequence targets in the spectra setting.

targets.target: continuous O-linear and Pontryagin duals with the correct compact/discrete topologies
targets.note: Mathlib defines the Pontryagin dual A →ₜ* Circle with the compact-open topology, with instances making the dual of a compact group discrete and of a discrete group compact. It also has the algebraic character module Hom(A, ℚ/ℤ) with exactness of dualization and the continuous linear dual. There is no continuous O-linear dual Hom_cont(M, O) or Hom_cont(M, E/O) with its topology for profinite O-modules.

targets.target: the dual of the smooth torsion colimit as a projective system, and completed homology lim_K H_i(Y(K), O) with the transfer direction
targets.note: No completed homology and no inverse limit of homology exist. Corestriction on group homology could supply transition maps.

targets.target: module structure of completed homology over O[[K₀]] for compact open K₀, distinguishing left modules from the opposite action arising by duality
targets.note: No completed group ring O[[K]] = lim O[K/U] exists. Mathlib's p-adic 'abstract measures' are continuous linear functionals C(ℤ_p, R) → E with the Amice transform D(ℤ_p, ℤ_p) ≃ ℤ_p⟦X⟧ as a linear equivalence only (no convolution product). The contragredient and the right-action-on-dual construction are purely algebraic.

targets.target: biduality in the compact/discrete or admissible category
targets.note: Biduality is proved only for finite abelian groups (with enough roots of unity) and for algebraically reflexive modules. Pontryagin duality for compact or discrete abelian groups, and duality between compact O[[K]]-modules and discrete torsion smooth modules, are absent.

targets.target: compatibility of continuous duals with localisation and completion
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves A ⊗_R Hom_R(M, R) ≅ Hom_A(A ⊗ M, A) for finite projective M, covering localisations. Nothing covers continuous duals of compact or completed modules.

duplicates.note: Declared supplier: defines R[[G]] = lim (R/Iⁿ)[G/U] with its topology and continuous module actions, the completed group ring over which CC.3 puts completed homology.
Also constructs O[[G]] as an inverse limit over open normal subgroups and coefficient quotients, with topology and continuous module actions, for p-adic Lie groups: the same object as CC.3's O[[K₀]].
Constructs the duals and completed group-algebra actions of the smooth mod-p and admissible Banach categories of GL₂(ℚ_p), the GL₂ case of CC.3's duality between compact and discrete objects.

targets.target: cellular complexes on finite CW or Borel–Serre models, and equivariant lifted cell complexes on a cofinal torsion-free tower (including boundary chains)
targets.note: CW complexes exist as topological structures, simplicial sets have chain complexes, and Tau Ceti realizes abstract simplicial complexes. There is no cellular chain complex, no G-CW complex and no Borel–Serre model.

targets.target: comparison of cellular with singular/étale cochains and compatibility of refinement maps
targets.note: Singular chains are defined as the simplicial chain complex of the singular set, which is a definition rather than a comparison theorem. No cellular–singular comparison exists.

targets.target: bounded complexes of finite free/projective O[[K₀]]-modules computing completed homology for a finite-cell compact quotient and compact p-adic analytic K₀
targets.note: Projective resolutions, K-projective complexes and finite resolutions in exact categories exist. There are no perfect complexes, no completed group rings and no finite free complexes computing completed homology.

targets.target: derived finite-level coinvariants recovering the finite-level complex (not underived invariants)
targets.note: For a discrete group G, Mathlib identifies group homology with Tor over k[G] (derived coinvariants) and proves Shapiro's lemma for homology. Derived coinvariants of complexes over O[[K₀]], and the recovery of the finite-level complex C ⊗^L_{O[[K₀]]} O[K₀/K], are absent.

duplicates.note: Builds bounded finite projective cellular models of the finite-level cochains under finite-CW and neat hypotheses, and compares singular/cellular cochains with sheaf cohomology: CC.4's finite-level chain models before the tower.
Defines cellular homology from skeleta and proves the cellular-to-singular comparison naturally up to specified homotopy, the generic form of CC.4's cellular–singular comparison.
Compares finite-level cellular complexes, algebraic local systems and integral Hecke actions with derived coefficient and level change, overlapping CC.4's finite-level chain-model comparisons.

Its manifold-with-corners Borel–Serre model, boundary fibrations and finite stratification are the Borel–Serre cell models on which CC.4's equivariant lifted cell complexes and boundary chains are built.

targets.target: noetherianity of the completed group algebra O[[K₀]] of a compact p-adic analytic group (Lazard)
targets.note: Mathlib proves power series rings in finitely many variables over a noetherian ring are noetherian, which would give O[[ℤ_pᵈ]] ≅ O[[T₁,…,T_d]]. Neither the completed group ring nor that isomorphism is formalized, and Mathlib's Amice transform is only a linear equivalence. Tau Ceti has the pro-p Frattini subgroup and topological finite generation. p-adic analytic, uniform or powerful groups and Lazard's theorem are absent.

targets.target: finite generation of completed homology over O[[K₀]] from the finite-cell tower model
targets.note: Only a complete Nakayama lemma for adically precomplete modules is available, which is an ingredient of the compact-module finiteness argument.

targets.target: dual admissibility criterion and admissibility of completed cohomology in the torsion and unitary Banach categories, with explicit finiteness hypotheses
targets.note: Neither library has admissible smooth or Banach representations; the searches found only unrelated uses of 'admissible' (quiver ideals, adic spaces).

duplicates.note: Proves the noetherian and module-finiteness facts for completed group rings of p-adic Lie groups under exact group hypotheses, the Lazard input CC.5 uses.
Proves the finiteness and compactness results for the admissible unitary Banach and smooth mod-p categories of GL₂(ℚ_p), the GL₂(ℚ_p) case of CC.5's admissibility category.

targets.target: continuous Hochschild–Serre (descent) spectral sequence comparing tower and fixed-level cohomology, with its edge maps
targets.note: Only the degree-one inflation–restriction exact sequence exists: for discrete groups (Mathlib) and for continuous cohomology with a normal subgroup (Tau Ceti). Spectral sequences and spectral objects exist as general frameworks, but Mathlib lists the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence as a TODO in GroupCohomology/Basic.lean.

targets.target: derived-invariants formulation of fixed-level cohomology and its functoriality for Hecke maps
targets.note: Mathlib defines continuous cohomology of topological groups with functoriality, and group cohomology of discrete groups as Ext (derived invariants). Tau Ceti shows H¹ of a profinite group is the colimit of the finite-level H¹. No derived functor RΓ(K, –) on smooth or completed coefficient modules exists, and nothing is functorial in Hecke correspondences.

targets.target: classical comparison maps for algebraic coefficient systems V via finite-level evaluation, with hypotheses and degree ranges
targets.note: Algebraic representations (symmetric powers; points of a Hopf algebra acting on a comodule) exist, but there is no map (H̃ ⊗ V)^K → H*(Y(K), V) and no locally algebraic vectors.

duplicates.note: The declared generic owner of full continuous Hochschild–Serre with convergence hypotheses and five-term/edge maps, which CC.6 applies to towers.
Proves finite-level descent and the finite-cover Hochschild–Serre application on the same tower, overlapping CC.6's descent comparison.

Relates classical finite-level cohomology with algebraic coefficients to completed cohomology for GL₂, the specialization of CC.6's classical comparison, and demands the same care about interchanging invariants and limits.

targets.target: the support triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_∂ passed through the derived tower construction: exactness and connecting morphisms
targets.note: The homological algebra exists: a short exact sequence of cochain complexes gives a distinguished triangle in the derived category and a long exact homology sequence with connecting maps (Mathlib), and Tau Ceti has the long exact sequence of a pair in singular homology. Compactly supported and boundary cohomology of arithmetic quotients, and their derived tower limits, are absent.

targets.target: relation of the derived limits with degreewise completed cohomology, including lim¹ and torsion errors
targets.note: No lim¹ or derived limit exists (see CC.2).

targets.target: completed interior cohomology as the specified image, with each comparison proved separately
targets.note: No interior, parabolic or cuspidal cohomology exists in either library, even at finite level (no Eichler–Shimura or modular-symbol cohomology).

duplicates.note: Declared supplier: proves the finite-level triangle RΓ_c → RΓ → RΓ_boundary → functorially in level and coefficients, which CC.7 passes through the tower.

Distinguishes ordinary, compactly supported and parabolic cohomology of modular curves at finite level and proves their comparisons: the modular-curve instance of CC.7's support and interior-cohomology targets.

targets.target: identification of the generic completed object with the finite-level modular, Siegel, unitary and Hilbert tower models
targets.note: Neither library has modular curves, Shimura, Siegel, unitary or Hilbert modular varieties as spaces or schemes. Only congruence subgroups and their proper action on ℍ exist.

targets.target: transport of finite-level Galois and tame Hecke actions, their continuity and commutation with all transition maps
targets.note: Pro-étale ℓ-adic cohomology of schemes is defined with no Galois action. No étale cohomology of Shimura varieties or Hecke action on it exists.

targets.target: localisation at a specified residual Hecke ideal (maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra)
targets.note: Tau Ceti maps the integral Hecke ring 𝕋(Δ₀(N), Γ₀(N), ℤ) to endomorphisms of the weight-k cusp forms with nebentypus χ, but does not form its image as a Hecke algebra 𝕋. Localisation at primes is general Mathlib. No Hecke algebra acting on tower cohomology, and no non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, exists.

targets.target: comparison with the conventions of Scholze's torsion paper §4.2 (support and lattice), exporting named comparison isomorphisms
targets.note: No completed cohomology exists in either library, so there is nothing to compare.

duplicates.note: Specializes CC.0–CC.8 to modular and Shimura curves, identifying the tower and transfer maps with ModularCurvesPartII and HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves: the GL₂ instance of CC.8's identification.
Constructs the finite and infinite Shimura towers with their group actions and level changes, the tower models CC.8 identifies with the generic completed object.
Proves torsion-freeness and finiteness of modular-curve cohomology after localising at a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal, the finite-level form of CC.8's localisation at a residual Hecke ideal.

GL2AutomorphicRepresentationsAndTransfer.summary: The libraries have a substantial classical GL₂/ℚ theory and nothing automorphic or local-representation-theoretic. Tau Ceti builds Atkin–Lehner–Li newform theory for S_k(Γ₁(N)): the old/new decomposition, newforms with a_n = λ_n and multiplicative coefficients, multiplicity one, and strong multiplicity one at fixed level and nebentypus. It also has Atkin–Lehner operators, Hecke rings with Shimura's GL₂ multiplication table, the representation theory of GL₂(𝔽_q) (principal series, Steinberg, elliptic induction), finite-group Clifford and Mackey theory, Schur multipliers with projective lifting, and quaternion norm forms and Brauer groups of ℝ and finite fields. Mathlib adds holomorphic q-expansions, Hecke's entire continuation of cusp-form L-functions via Mellin transforms, Haar measure on locally compact groups, and local compactness of restricted products. Everything the roadmap actually targets is missing: GL₂(𝔸_F) and automorphic representations, smooth admissible representations of GL₂ over local fields and their classification, local newvectors, local Langlands and Weil–Deligne data, the converse theorem, local and global Jacquet–Langlands, Hilbert symbols and Hasse invariants, trace formulas, base change, automorphic induction and Langlands–Tunnell. Every layer is not built; the classical newform theory reported here must not be planned again.

targets.target: GL₂ over local fields and over 𝔸_F as locally compact groups, specializing the generic restricted-product and reductive-group constructions
targets.note: The ingredients exist. A restricted product of locally compact groups over open subgroups, compact for cofinitely many factors, is locally compact. Units of a locally compact T₁ topological monoid form a locally compact group (an unnamed instance in Mathlib/Topology/Algebra/Group/Units.lean), which covers GL₂(F_v) = M₂(F_v)ˣ. Finite completions of a number field are nonarchimedean local fields (Tau Ceti). GL₂(𝔸_F) is not assembled as a topological group, and `RestrictedProduct.unitsEquiv` is only a monoid isomorphism, not a homeomorphism.

targets.target: the chosen compact subgroups GL₂(𝒪_v), O(2) and U(2), and the adelic congruence subgroups K₀(N) and K₁(N), with their Iwasawa and Cartan decompositions
targets.note: Compactness of GL₂(𝒪_v) follows from Mathlib's compact 𝒪_v and compact submonoid units, and Tau Ceti proves unitary groups compact (so O(n), U(n)). HabiroNahmSeries.summary: Towards this roadmap the libraries have the classical modular side and generic analytic and algebraic tools, but none of its objects. Mathlib has finite-index (arithmetic) subgroups of SL₂(ℤ) without a congruence hypothesis, their cusps (ℙ¹(ℚ)) with scaling matrices and finitely many cusp orbits, q-parameters and holomorphic q-expansions, meromorphic orders and trailing coefficients, the Dedekind eta product with its S-transformation, the pentagonal number theorem and Euler partition identities, multipliability of formal and analytic infinite products, Gaussian integrals, Stirling's formula, Witt-vector ghost maps and Frobenius on power series. Tau Ceti adds widths and vanishing orders at every cusp of a finite-index subgroup (with the general-level valence formula) and multivariate Gaussian densities. Genuinely missing: Nahm equations and their algebraic solutions, pre-Bloch/Bloch groups and dilogarithms, finite q-Pochhammer symbols and Nahm sums, Euler–Maclaurin and saddle-point asymptotics, meromorphic modular functions with Laurent expansions at cusps, the modularity-implies-torsion theorem, GSWZ admissible series with finite support, Dwork-type Frobenius congruences, Habiro rings and modules, and explicit GSWZ examples. HB.5a is the only layer with a fully present target (finite-index subgroups and their cusps and widths).

targets.target: one rational and one nonabelian number-field example from GSWZ: exact field presentation, verified nondegenerate solution, Bloch/K₃ class, excluded primes, first coefficients and the module-membership proof
targets.note: Only generic explicit-field tools exist (a prime-degree ℚ-polynomial with few nonreal roots has full Galois group, and Tau Ceti's multiquadratic degree examples). No GSWZ example, Bloch/K₃ class or Nahm solution exists.

targets.target: a rank-one product identity checking the q-difference and admissibility conventions
targets.note: Mathlib proves Euler's pentagonal number theorem (formal and analytic) and the odd-parts/distinct-parts identity. Neither is a Nahm-sum = product identity, so it cannot check the q-difference or admissibility conventions. Euler's Σ q^{n(n−1)/2}xⁿ/(q)_n = (−x;q)_∞, the q-binomial theorem and Rogers–Ramanujan are absent.

targets.note: Tau Ceti has the Jones representation of braid groups (without Markov trace) and the Alexander polynomial of Seifert matrices. There are no colored Jones polynomials, Kashaev invariants, perturbative series or quantum modularity.

targets.note: Mathlib has every ingredient: the structure theorem G ≃ ℤⁿ × ⨁ ZMod(p^e) for finitely generated abelian groups, freeness of finitely generated torsion-free modules over a PID, 'm ∣ x and |x| < m ⇒ x = 0', and Krull intersection. The lemma itself (an element of nG for unboundedly many n is torsion) is not stated.

targets.target: finiteness of the primes excluded by the exceptional integer, and verification that the orders used by the modular argument satisfy the arithmetic hypotheses
targets.note: The exceptional integer comes from the K₃/Chern-class comparison, none of which exists.

targets.target: use of the finite Chern-class and cyclic-dilogarithm identities with the good-order injectivity results
targets.note: Only the K₁ analogue exists: reduction modulo the maximal ideal of a local ring is injective on n-th roots of unity for n a unit (Tau Ceti). No Chern classes or cyclic dilogarithm exist.

duplicates.note: Declared supplier: proves the injectivity/isomorphism results for the finite Chern class under the precise good-order hypotheses that HB.5's final argument invokes.

The same layer supplies the cyclic-dilogarithm and finite-Chern-class identities under the good-order hypotheses HB.5's final argument uses; HB.1, already listed, supplies only the injectivity/isomorphism results for the Chern class.

targets.target: finite-index subgroups Γ of SL₂(ℤ), not assumed to be congruence subgroups
targets.note: Mathlib's modular-forms API is stated for arithmetic subgroups of GL₂(ℝ) (commensurable with SL₂(ℤ)). For Γ ≤ SL₂(ℤ) this is exactly finite index, with the congruence property a separate predicate, so the non-congruence generality the layer insists on is already the default.

targets.target: rational cusps, cusp widths and scaling matrices
targets.note: Mathlib: cusps are points fixed by a parabolic element, the cusps of any arithmetic subgroup are ℙ¹(ℚ), every cusp is g•∞ with g ∈ SL₂(ℤ) (a scaling matrix), and an arithmetic subgroup has finitely many cusp orbits (unnamed instance). The width at ∞ is `Subgroup.strictWidthInfty`. Tau Ceti: widths at every cusp via ⟨T⟩-orbits on SL₂(ℤ)/Γ, the least m > 0 with x⁻¹Tᵐx ∈ Γ. This is the classical width of x⁻¹∞ when −I ∈ Γ, and otherwise that width or twice it; the widths sum to the index.

targets.target: weight-zero Γ-invariant meromorphic functions with meromorphic expansions (finite principal part) at every cusp
targets.note: Weight-0 slash-invariant forms are Γ-invariant functions with no analytic condition. Holomorphic modular forms have q-expansions and vanishing orders at cusps (Tau Ceti), and Mathlib proves weight-0 holomorphic forms constant. Mathlib also has orders of meromorphic functions. Meromorphic or weakly holomorphic modular functions, i.e. meromorphic at every cusp with Laurent q-expansions, are not defined.

targets.target: the local parameter q_c = exp(2πiz/w_c), transformation under a scaling matrix, and the Laurent expansion with finite principal part
targets.note: Mathlib has qParam h z = exp(2πiz/h) with ‖q‖ = exp(−2π Im z/h), the equivalence IsZeroAt (g•c) f ↔ IsZeroAt c (f∣g) (transport to ∞ by a scaling matrix), and power-series q-expansions of holomorphic bounded periodic functions. Tau Ceti reads each cusp in its own width. Laurent q-expansions with a finite principal part (meromorphic at the cusp) are absent.

targets.target: along the radial approach, the rational π² exponential growth rate from the leading Laurent exponent and rational cusp data, selecting the first nonzero coefficient and separating the identically zero case
targets.note: For holomorphic periodic functions there are exponential decay f − f(i∞) = O(exp(−2π Im τ/h)), and O(‖q‖ᴺ) when the first N coefficients vanish. For meromorphic functions, (z−x)^{−ord} f tends to the leading coefficient, with order ⊤ exactly for the identically zero germ. These do the 'first nonzero Laurent term' bookkeeping, but the radial growth theorem at a cusp of a modular function is absent.

duplicates.note: Its general-level valence formula for finite-index subgroups uses cusp widths and orders at every cusp, read through the coset norm. Tau Ceti has built this cusp infrastructure (`valence_formula_finiteIndex`), and HB.5a should reuse it rather than rebuild cusps and widths.

targets.target: admissible multivariable series: existence and uniqueness of the product expansion ∏(1 − q^{i/2}xⁿ)^{c_{n,i}} with integer exponents in the completed ring, with its support conditions
targets.note: Mathlib gives existence of infinite products of multivariable power series 1 + fᵢ once the weighted order tends to ∞, formal partition-type products, the one-variable formal logarithm, (1+X)^r for binomial exponents, and Möbius inversion (to recover exponents from logarithmic coefficients). Uniqueness of the product expansion (the plethystic/Euler transform) and multivariable formal logarithms are absent.

targets.target: GSWZ's series F_A for a symmetric integral matrix A, its q-difference equations, and Lemma 2.6 by the formal Gaussian/q-difference calculation
targets.note: Only generic tools exist: substitution f(X) ↦ f(aX) (a q-shift when a = q) and uniqueness for recursive equations f = g·f with g(0) = 0. No q-difference operators or formal Gaussian integrals exist.

targets.target: GSWZ Theorem 6: for each fixed nonzero n only finitely many i have c_{n,i} ≠ 0, via the Laurent-polynomial coefficient recurrence and cancellation of cyclotomic poles
targets.note: Laurent polynomials, ∏_{d∣n} Φ_d = Xⁿ − 1 and coprimality of distinct cyclotomic polynomials over ℚ exist; no DT-type integrality or finite-support theorem does.

duplicates.note: Proves coefficientwise finiteness of infinite products in formal power series rings, the existence half of HB.8's product-expansion target.

targets.target: GSWZ Theorem 4 (Frobenius congruence): log F(x^p, q^p) − p·log F(x, q) lies in the stated (p/x)-multiple of the completed coefficient ring, tracking fractional powers, residue classes mod m and m-th roots

review.notes: Re-checked the whole batch against the pinned baseline (mathlib 082e2d3, tauceti f790474): 5 roadmaps, 41 layers, 169 targets, 411 declaration citations naming 374 distinct declarations, and 104 duplicate claims. No target changed library, no note needed repair and no verdict moved; the corrections are 15 duplicates the audit had not found. Presence claims: all 61 targets that claim something is in the libraries (5 mathlib, 2 both, 54 partial) were re-derived from the source. Every citation resolves at its stated library, file and line; none is private, an axiom or a bare structure field; `grep -n sorry` is clean in all 374 cited files (the two hits in Mathlib/GroupTheory/FiniteAbelian/Basic.lean sit inside a TODO comment block, not in a declaration). Three citations are absent from declarations.tsv but present in the sources exactly as described (ModularForm.weakFEPair, ModularForm.Λ, Topology.RelCWComplex). Hypotheses and generality were checked against each target: hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le really is over an RCLike parameter, so holomorphic dependence is included; Fourier.fourierIntegral really is defined for any CommRing while every theorem from line 417 of FourierTransform.lean carries [InnerProductSpace ℝ V] [FiniteDimensional ℝ V]; haarMeasure_quotient really carries [Subgroup.Normal Γ] [Countable Γ], which is why the non-normal quotient GL₂(F)Z(𝔸)\GL₂(𝔸) is correctly called missing; groupCohomology.coindIso holds for every subgroup and Rep.indCoindIso for finite index, so CC.0's level-change claim is sound; polynomialRingEquivTwo is Shimura Theorem 3.20 for n = 1, 2 only, as the note says. Absence and partial claims: 81 of the 108 'absent' targets were re-searched independently by concept, by Mathlib naming convention and by grep of both Lean trees, together with the missing half of each of the 54 'partial' targets. Every claim held. Confirmed absent from both libraries: Schwartz–Bruhat spaces, self-dual local measures, adelic Poisson summation, Tate/Godement–Jacquet/Rankin–Selberg zeta integrals, ε- and γ-factors, Satake and L-groups, Weil–Deligne data and local Langlands, Whittaker and Kirillov models, converse theorems, trace-class/Hilbert–Schmidt/Schatten/nuclear operators, direct integrals and spectral measures, Arthur truncation and Maass–Selberg, orbital integrals and every trace formula, weighted cohomology and Franke's comparison, lim¹ and the Milnor sequence, Mittag-Leffler for module systems, the Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence (a TODO in GroupCohomology/Basic.lean), cellular homology and singular cohomology, Borel–Serre, perfect complexes, completed group rings and Lazard's theorem, admissible smooth or Banach representations, locally algebraic vectors, modular curves and Shimura varieties, Galois representations of modular forms, Jacquet–Langlands and quaternionic forms, Brandt matrices and Eichler orders, the Hilbert symbol and Hasse invariants, base change and automorphic induction, Langlands–Tunnell and Rohrlich–Tunnell, q-Pochhammer symbols and q-binomials (a TODO in RingTheory/Polynomial/Pochhammer.lean), Li₂ and the Bloch–Wigner and cyclic dilogarithms, Bloch groups and the five-term relation, Euler–Maclaurin and saddle-point asymptotics, Nahm and Habiro objects, Dieudonné–Dwork and Artin–Hasse. Two searches that could plausibly have overturned a claim and did not: Mathlib's p-adic AbstractMeasure carries no Mul or Ring instance and no convolution, and amiceTransformEquiv is only a linear equivalence D(ℤ_p,ℤ_p) ≃ₗ ℤ_p⟦X⟧, so it is not the completed group ring O[[ℤ_p]] and CC.3's and CC.5's claims stand; Mathlib's convexity API has only the one-variable strictConvexOn_of_deriv2_pos, with no positive-definite-Hessian criterion, so HB.3's note is right. Verdicts: 35 not built, 6 partly built, none built or process. All 7 fully present targets sit in 'partly built' layers and every 'not built' layer has no present target, so the verdicts are consistent with the targets. The target lists faithfully decompose the layer descriptions in the extracts; no stated target is missing. CC.0's derived group-cohomology target is the one presence claim that reads generously, since its arithmetic-group input does not exist, but the model itself is in Mathlib for any group and the note says so, so 'mathlib' is the right message: do not rebuild group cohomology. Duplicates: all 104 original claims resolve to live atlas stages (85 roadmap layers and 19 Tau Ceti roadmap anchors); none belongs to the retired FoundationsAndLibraryIntegration and none is self-referential. The four hidden HabiroNahmSeries KU-* stages are correctly omitted. The 15 added duplicates are listed above; the sharpest are QuadraticFormInvariants 6C, which owns the Hilbert symbol and local Hasse invariant R17.1 needs, ArithmeticLocallySymmetricSpaces ALS.2, which is the Borel–Serre compactification CC.0 and CC.4 build on, StableHomotopyKTheory H.6, which constructs the Milnor lim¹ sequence CC.2 asks for, and HabiroNumberFields HB.2, which owns the cyclic quantum dilogarithm HB.4 and HB.5 invoke.
